newsitem.title: UK: Top UK soccer clubs mull own TV service -FT.
newsitem.headline: Top UK soccer clubs mull own TV service -FT.

text.p: England's top soccer clubs have been advised to set up their own television service when a deal with satellite broadcaster BSkyB expires in 2001, the Financial Times said on Tuesday.

The newspaper said an interim report to the Premier League clubs calculated top soccer will be worth 1.3 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) to BSkyB over the next four years, twice the 670 million pounds it is paying to show live Premiership football over this period.

If the league is to benefit fully from its popularity it should consider setting up a dedicated Premier League pay-TV service in 2001 and receive all the revenues generated by coverage of matches, instead of sharing them with BSkyB.
